Ethos & Aims
Our vision is to form young people of academic excellence, character and integrity who shape society through service, joy, and responsibility.
College motto
College principal virtues
How we do it
We form each young person to be ready to contribute meaningfully to society by:
building intellectual curiosity and interdependence
sustaining a College environment that is calm, courteous, and orderly
providing a rigorous and ambitious academic curriculum
cultivating freedom with responsibility
Tutorial System
The personalised Tutorial System is the most distinctive feature of Fidelis College. The goal of the tutorial system is to help each pupil reach their potential in every area of their life. Tutors stay in close contact with parents throughout the year.
The principal area of education which the tutorial system addresses is the pupil’s character. Everything else, including academic results, flows from this. Academic results are part of a bigger picture. The Fidelis’ aim is to work with parents in the education of the whole person academically, spiritually, culturally, socially and physically.
Tutorial Discussion Points
Studies
During the school years character will be largely formed by the approach to schoolwork.
Social Development
Contribution to the wider society with generosity and understanding is important. We aim to foster an attitude of service.
Character development
The tutor aims to use every opportunity to encourage the pupil to develop character and they do this hand in hand with the Virtues Programme in place at the school.
Catholic character
Chaplaincy & Catholic identity
The chaplaincy, composed of priests from Opus Dei, is responsible for accompanying, guiding, and providing spiritual and pastoral support to students, families, friends, alumni, and members of staff. Through regular opportunities for prayer, reflection, and sacramental life, the chaplaincy plays a central role in nurturing the spiritual development of the whole school community.
The school chapel is always open, offering a quiet and reverent space for personal prayer throughout the day. Holy Mass is celebrated daily and is available to pupils who wish to attend. The Sacrament of Reconciliation is also available daily, ensuring that pupils and members of the wider community have regular and easy access to confession.
House System
At Fidelis College, the House System is a central pillar of school life, fostering community, leadership, friendship, and healthy competition across all year groups. Every pupil and member of staff is assigned to one of four Houses:
Each house is a vibrant community, offering pupils the chance to contribute, compete, lead and belong throughout their time at Fidelis.

Welcome to Admissions
Begin Your Journey with Us
Join one of our Open Events
Reception
The Beginning of a Purposeful Education
Step 1 | Enquiry & Tour
Sign up to an Open event or a smaller and more personal weekday tour. Parents will be offered a follow up meeting with our Head of Prep. Contact a member of the Admissions Team on: 020 8185 7770
Choosing a school is a significant decision for your whole family. Our aim is that you leave with a clear understanding of our strong academic standards, and how our character development approach underpins and strengthens every aspect of school life. Join Weekday Tour
Step 2 | Application
Step 3 | Assessment Day and Parent Interview
Parent interview: We believe parents are the prime educators of their children, therefore you will be invited to a parent interview so we can learn more about your family, your child and the hopes you hold for them.
Child centred: We also visit children at their current nursery and speak with their key worker to gain a broader picture of their development. This approach is proven to make the transition from nursery to school seamless. A written reference will also be requested.
If your child does not attend nursery, or if a visit is not possible, we will arrange an alternative opportunity to spend time with them in our school environment.
Step 4 | Offer & Enrolment
Families who accept a place will then be invited to meet the class teacher and children will be invited to attend taster mornings, ensuring your child feels known and confident for their first day of school.

Step 3 | Assessment Day and Parent Interview
There are two parts to our assessment process.
Parent interview We believe parents are the prime educators of their children. You will be invited to a meeting so we can learn more about your child’s current experience, their strengths, and the aspirations you hold for them.
Pupil assessment Your child will be invited to spend a day with us from 9.15am to 3.50pm. They will complete age appropriate standardised assessments in English and mathematics, as well as join the class for the remainder of the day.
This will allow your child to experience the school day and meet their peers and teachers. It also enables us to see how they approach learning and engage with others. A written reference from your child’s current school will also be requested.
This process helps ensure that Fidelis Prep is the right environment for your child to continue to flourish.
Step 4 | Offer & Enrolment
Families who accept a place will then be invited to meet the class teacher and children will be invited to attend a transition morning, ensuring all new children feel known and confident for their first day of school.

Sixth Form
Preparing for Future Success
Step 1 | Enquiry & Application
Families are encouraged to contact the Admissions Team to make an inquiry into Sixth Form. Prospective students may attend a College Open Morning or arrange an individual visit to meet staff and learn more about subject pathways, enrichment and university preparation. For current pupils wishing to join Sixth Form we will have a dedicated Sixth Form Open and Options Evening in early October.
Step 2 | Application
External Applicants External candidates apply via the online Admissions Portal or by contacting admissions@fidelis.org.uk. Early application is advised to support subject planning. Late applications are considered subject to availability and course viability.
Step 3 | Assessment & Interview
External applicants whose predicted grades suggest they are likely to meet entry requirements are invited to interview with the Head of Sixth Form. This discussion explores subject choices, academic readiness and commitment to Sixth Form study. Academic references from the applicant’s current school will be requested.
Internal applicants do not require a formal interview, though course guidance conversations may take place where appropriate.
Step 4 | Entry Requirments
In order to meet the academic demands of A-Levels applicants to Fidelis Sixth Form must achieve:
• Grade 7 or above in subjects to be studied at A Level • Grade 8 in Mathematics for Further Mathematics • Grade 4 or above in English Language or Literature and Mathematics
Some subjects have additional requirements; please consult individual course pages.
All offers are conditional upon the GCSE results in August. Subject combinations are confirmed following results and remain subject to timetabling and course viability.
Step 5 | Scholarships & Bursaries
Academic Scholarships are awarded on the basis of GCSE performance and are determined following the publication of GCSE results.
Means-tested bursaries are available through the Bursary; families should contact the Bursar (bursar@fidelis.org.uk) for further information.
Step 6 | Offer & Enrolment
External applicants Offers are made following review of the application, predicted grades and interview.
Internal applicants Offers are presumed unless otherwise stated, subject to meeting the published entry requirements.
All successful applicants, internal and external, will attend a dedicated Induction Day on Wednesday 17 June 2026 to support preparation for transition to A Level and post-16 study.
Formal enrolment takes place on Thursday 20th August once GCSE results are confirmed.
Frequently Asked Questions
What are the main entry points?
We welcome pupils at several key stages, including Early Years, 7+, 11+ and Sixth Form. Entry at other points may also be possible, subject to availability. Our admissions team will always take the time to talk through the most appropriate entry point for your child and advise on next steps.
Why choose Fidelis College for my child's education?
Families choose Fidelis because we combine high academic expectations with genuine personal care. We take the time to know each pupil as an individual and to support them academically, pastorally, and spiritually. Our aim is not simply exam success, but to help young people grow into confident, compassionate, and resilient individuals.
What kind of child thrives at Fidelis College?
There is no single “type” of Fidelis pupil. Our students are curious, kind, and willing to grow — whether they arrive confident and outgoing or quieter and still finding their voice. What matters most is a readiness to engage, to try, and to develop both character and intellect within a supportive community.
What does ‘character-first’ actually look like day to day?
Character is woven into everyday school life, not added on. Through tutor time, assemblies, service opportunities, and daily interactions, pupils are encouraged to show joy, courage, responsibility, and service. Staff model these values consistently, helping pupils develop strong habits, self-awareness, and respect for others.
How Catholic is the school?
Fidelis College is proudly Catholic, with faith and values at the heart of school life. Our ethos shapes how we care for pupils and treat one another. Catholic families are fully supported in their faith journey, and families of other faiths — or none — are warmly welcomed and respected. Our focus is on shared values, understanding, and community.
How involved are parents?
We see education as a partnership. Parents are kept well informed and are encouraged to engage with school life, whether through communication with tutors, attending events, or sharing insights that help us support their child. We value open dialogue and believe that strong relationships between home and school make a real difference.

Sixth Form
Preparing for Future Success
Step 1 | Enquiry & Application
Families are encouraged to contact the Admissions Team to make an inquiry into Sixth Form. Prospective students may attend a College Open Morning or arrange an individual visit to meet staff and learn more about subject pathways, enrichment and university preparation. For current pupils wishing to join Sixth Form we will have a dedicated Sixth Form Open and Options Evening in early October.
Step 2 | Application
External Applicants External candidates apply via the online Admissions Portal or by contacting admissions@fidelis.org.uk. Early application is advised to support subject planning. Late applications are considered subject to availability and course viability.
Step 3 | Assessment & Interview
External applicants whose predicted grades suggest they are likely to meet entry requirements are invited to interview with the Head of Sixth Form. This discussion explores subject choices, academic readiness and commitment to Sixth Form study. Academic references from the applicant’s current school will be requested.
Internal applicants do not require a formal interview, though course guidance conversations may take place where appropriate.
Step 4 | Entry Requirments
In order to meet the academic demands of A-Levels applicants to Fidelis Sixth Form must achieve:
• Grade 7 or above in subjects to be studied at A Level • Grade 8 in Mathematics for Further Mathematics • Grade 4 or above in English Language or Literature and Mathematics
Some subjects have additional requirements; please consult individual course pages.
All offers are conditional upon the GCSE results in August. Subject combinations are confirmed following results and remain subject to timetabling and course viability.
Step 5 | Scholarships & Bursaries
Academic Scholarships are awarded on the basis of GCSE performance and are determined following the publication of GCSE results.
Means-tested bursaries are available through the Bursary; families should contact the Bursar (bursar@fidelis.org.uk) for further information.
Step 6 | Offer & Enrolment
External applicants Offers are made following review of the application, predicted grades and interview.
Internal applicants Offers are presumed unless otherwise stated, subject to meeting the published entry requirements.
All successful applicants, internal and external, will attend a dedicated Induction Day on Wednesday 17 June 2026 to support preparation for transition to A Level and post-16 study.
Formal enrolment takes place on Thursday 20th August once GCSE results are confirmed.
Frequently Asked Questions
What are the main entry points?
We welcome pupils at several key stages, including Early Years, 7+, 11+ and Sixth Form. Entry at other points may also be possible, subject to availability. Our admissions team will always take the time to talk through the most appropriate entry point for your child and advise on next steps.
Why choose Fidelis College for my child's education?
Families choose Fidelis because we combine high academic expectations with genuine personal care. We take the time to know each pupil as an individual and to support them academically, pastorally, and spiritually. Our aim is not simply exam success, but to help young people grow into confident, compassionate, and resilient individuals.
What kind of child thrives at Fidelis College?
There is no single “type” of Fidelis pupil. Our students are curious, kind, and willing to grow — whether they arrive confident and outgoing or quieter and still finding their voice. What matters most is a readiness to engage, to try, and to develop both character and intellect within a supportive community.
What does ‘character-first’ actually look like day to day?
Character is woven into everyday school life, not added on. Through tutor time, assemblies, service opportunities, and daily interactions, pupils are encouraged to show joy, courage, responsibility, and service. Staff model these values consistently, helping pupils develop strong habits, self-awareness, and respect for others.
How Catholic is the school?
Fidelis College is proudly Catholic, with faith and values at the heart of school life. Our ethos shapes how we care for pupils and treat one another. Catholic families are fully supported in their faith journey, and families of other faiths — or none — are warmly welcomed and respected. Our focus is on shared values, understanding, and community.
How involved are parents?
We see education as a partnership. Parents are kept well informed and are encouraged to engage with school life, whether through communication with tutors, attending events, or sharing insights that help us support their child. We value open dialogue and believe that strong relationships between home and school make a real difference.

Mrs Nuria FontInternational Coordinator
International Coordinator’s Welcome
As a mother of eight children who have all benefited from a Fidelis education, and with ten years leading Fidelis International, I understand how important it is to know that your child is safe, happy and well cared for.
I personally support each student and family, acting as the link between home, school and carefully selected host families. Wherever possible, students are matched with families who have children of a similar age, helping them feel at home from the outset.
For longer stays, I also coordinate all Private Fostering arrangements and safeguarding requirements with the local council and AEGIS.
Above all, every child’s wellbeing comes first. My aim is simple: for your child to feel safe, valued and truly at home.
AEGIS
AEGIS is an independent UK charity that safeguards international students by inspecting and accrediting educational guardianship organisations. Its standards help schools and parents identify guardians who provide appropriate care, welfare support and emergency arrangements for students studying away from home.
Our International Programme
kid_star
Character Development Programme

It builds confidence, responsibility, and encourages children to seek goodness in themselves and others, supporting academic achievement and personal growth. Through assemblies, tutorials, lessons and daily routines, we teach virtues such as respect, gratitude, perseverance and courage. Pupils reflect on their behaviour and grow in self-knowledge.
social_leaderboard

Curriculum

In addition to the regular curriculum followed, students receive additional English as a foreign language classes to help prepare them for The Cambridge Exam which they will usually sit during their stay.
celebration

Fidelis Prep
First Steps into Your Child’s Learning Journey
Head’s Welcome
Our academic standards are upheld by our Character Development programme, this unique programme ensures that every child is able to fulfill their academic potential. It is the foundation which enables pupils to think deeply, be ambitious learners and persevere when learning becomes demanding. Our tutorial system guides each child to discover the beauty and depth of each person starting through knowing themselves. Our small classes, broad curriculum and individual attention provides the best possible education for your child.
We follow our school motto with pride, In gaudio serviamus, We Serve with Joy. We want our pupils to recognise the gifts they have been given and to use them generously. In doing so, they develop a strong moral compass that will guide them long beyond their years at Prep and shape the way they contribute to the world.
The Fidelis Way
The Fidelis Way in the Prep School is rooted in high expectations, kindness and curiosity, ensuring every child feels known, valued and inspired to grow in confidence, character and academic ambition within a nurturing and purposeful community.
kid_star
Character Development Programme
Character education lies at the heart of our school. It builds confidence, responsibility, and encourages children to seek goodness in themselves and others, supporting academic achievement and personal growth. Through assemblies, tutorials, lessons and daily routines, we teach virtues such as respect, gratitude, perseverance and courage. Pupils reflect on their behaviour and grow in self-knowledge.
Each week, one child per class becomes the Secret Agent, quietly observing which classmate best exemplifies the weekly virtue. In Friday’s assemble, Secret Agents reveal themselves and share their observations, awarding the Character Star to a deserving peer.
social_leaderboard
Pupil Leadership Roles
Children of all ages are encouraged to take on responsibilities, nurturing service, pride and belonging. Year 6 pupils assume leadership roles such as Head Girl, Head Boy, House Captains, and ambassador positions in areas like health and safety, reading, the arts and peer friendships – offering opportunities for older pupils to lead with generosity and maturity.
Tutorials & Mentoring Programme
Our unique mentoring programme assigns tutors to pupils in addition to their class teachers. Tutors guide, encourage, and help children personalise their character development. Tutorials take place every two weeks, allowing for open discussions on progress, relationships, goals and challenges. Group tutorials provide a wider forum for discussion, while individual tutorials occur in open, informal spaces.
Older pupils (Years 4-6) receive dedicated tutor support, while Year 3 pupils are paired with trained Sixth Form mentors as role models and companions. This approach supports parents in their role as primary educators.
celebration
Celebrating Achievements
We take pride in recognising each child’s efforts, progress and personal growth. Weekly whole-school and good work assemblies, character stars, merit badges, house points, certificates and termly commendations celebrate excellence and development. Our annual Prizegiving Awards Ceremony honours achievements across all year groups.
Why our Curriculum Stands out
The Fidelis Prep Curriculum
Our core subjects are English, Mathematics, Science and Religious Education. Pupils also study History, Geography, French, Spanish, Art, Music, Physical Education (PE), Character Development and Relationship Health Education (RHE). Latin is introduced in Years 5 and 6.
We foster curiosity, critical thinking, creativity, reflective discussion, communication and resilience across all subjects. Pupils are encouraged to ask questions, explore ideas and reflect on their learning.
The Reception Curriculum follows the Early Years Framework’s seven areas of learning, nurturing key behaviours: Playing and Exploring, Active Learning, and Creating and Thinking Critically. These are supported by purposeful play, adult-guided learning and high quality interactions.
Our Concept Curriculum (Reception to Year 2) enables children to ask meaningful questions, challenge assumptions and explore big ideas, building confidence and supporting academic and personal development. Each term is centred on a key concept – such as Identity, Change or Journeys – creating deep connections across subjects.
PE is taught by specialist sports teachers, with pupils in Years 3-6 participating in fixtures throughout the year, and all pupils enjoying swimming and Sports Day in the summer term.
The Fidelis Pupil Experience
We encourage pupils to develop new interests through a variety of clubs and enrichment opportunities. Our free afterschool club programme (Monday-Thursday, 15:50-16:45) is tailored for Reception to Year 6, while a breakfast club runs daily from 08:00-08:30.
Pupils take part in local and national competitions, challenging themselves in poetry, public speaking, mathematics, engineering, science, writing, sport and the arts.
Educational trips and visits enrich the curriculum and are closely linked to topic work, with outings to museums, galleries, nature reserves, historical sites, theatres, farms and botanical gardens. Visiting workshops and speakers further enhance learning.
Partnership with Parents
Strong communication and partnership between home and school are vital for pupil success at Fidelis Prep. Families receive regular updates via the Seesaw platform, daily check-ins, termly meetings, written reports and Friday bulletins. Class charts help parents stay informed and involved.
We host events throughout the year to build community and celebrate achievements, including assemblies, exhibitions, class productions, and Friends of Fidelis events. Parents are welcome to volunteer and join parent-only events such as Quiz Nights and the Marriage MOT Conference.
Two formal parents’ evenings are held annually, with additional meetings available as needed. Academic progress and attitudes to learning are reported in the autumn and spring terms, with a detailed report at the end of the summer term.
Homework is set to reinforce learning and build study habits, ranging from optional 20-minute sessions in Reception to an hour in Years 5 and 6, with weekly tasks in English and Maths.
